title: Count Before You Clamp
setup: The King's Indian Attack setup is complete, and Black has just pushed a pawn to b6 with a bishop on d6. Play the central push this setup was built for.
hint: One push grabs space and offers a pawn at the same time. Count attackers and defenders on that square before you commit.
explanation:
## The Idea

{{e5}} is the push every King's Indian Attack is built around, and it gains space with tempo on the bishop.

It also offers a pawn, and taking is a mistake. e5 is attacked by the bishop on d6 and the knight on c6, and defended by the knight on f3 and the rook on e1. After {{Bxe5}} {{Nxe5}} {{Nxe5}} {{Rxe5}}, White is a bishop for a pawn up. Black's best is to step the bishop back and concede the space.

Count what each attacker is worth, not just how many.
